provenance.method: Concept list and short descriptions written by an agent from the lecture-note headings (knowledge_graph/curriculum.json), the Dembo subsection scope (knowledge_graph/course_scope/stats310a-autumn-2026.json) and general mathematical knowledge. prerequisite.meaning: Source is needed to state or understand the target.

used_in_proof.meaning: Source is a step or tool in a standard proof of the target.

generalizes.meaning: Source is a more general statement; the target is a special case.

equivalent_formulation.meaning: The two express the same mathematical content in different terms.

application.meaning: Target is an application or consequence obtained by applying the source.

shares_structure.meaning: Both concern the same mathematical object or structure, without a dependency.

counterexample.meaning: Source is an example showing that a hypothesis of, or a converse to, the target fails.

concepts.name: σ-algebra
concepts.summary: A collection F of subsets of Ω containing Ω and closed under complements and countable unions; the domain on which a measure is defined. Countable operations stay inside F, and unions can be disjointized.

concepts.name: Measure
concepts.summary: A map μ: F → [0,∞] with μ(∅)=0 that is countably additive on disjoint sets: μ(⋃A_n)=Σμ(A_n). The triple (Ω,F,μ) is a measure space; μ is finite, σ-finite, or atomless depending on its masses.

concepts.name: Probability space
concepts.summary: A measure space (Ω,F,P) with total mass P(Ω)=1. Events are sets in F and P assigns them probabilities; every statement about random variables is ultimately a statement about P on F.

concepts.name: Algebra of sets
concepts.summary: A collection closed under complements and finite unions, such as finite disjoint unions of intervals. A premeasure that is countably additive on an algebra is the input to Carathéodory extension.

concepts.name: Continuity of measure
concepts.summary: For increasing events A_n ↑ A, μ(A_n) ↑ μ(A); for decreasing A_n ↓ A with μ(A_1)<∞, μ(A_n) ↓ μ(A). The finite-mass caveat matters: A_n=[n,∞) under Lebesgue measure.

concepts.name: Non-measurable sets
aliases: why volume cannot be assigned to every set
concepts.summary: Using the axiom of choice, a translation-invariant, countably additive length cannot be defined on every subset of [0,1). This forces measures to live on a σ-algebra rather than the full power set.

concepts.name: Generated σ-algebra
concepts.summary: σ(A) is the intersection of all σ-algebras containing the class A: the smallest σ-algebra containing it. Proofs about σ(A) usually check a property on generators and show the good sets form a σ-algebra.

concepts.name: Borel σ-algebra
concepts.summary: The σ-algebra generated by the open sets of a topological space. On R it is generated by intervals (a,b] with rational endpoints, or by half-lines (-∞,x], a countable generating class.

concepts.name: π-system
concepts.summary: A nonempty class of sets closed under finite intersections, such as half-lines (-∞,x] or measurable rectangles. Two finite measures agreeing on a π-system agree on the σ-algebra it generates.

concepts.name: λ-system
concepts.summary: A class containing Ω, closed under proper differences B∖A for A⊆B, and under increasing unions. A class that is both a π-system and a λ-system is a σ-algebra.

concepts.name: π–λ theorem
concepts.summary: If P is a π-system contained in a λ-system L, then σ(P) ⊆ L. It turns a property verified on an intersection-closed generating class into a property of the whole generated σ-algebra.

concepts.name: Uniqueness of measures
concepts.summary: Two measures that agree on a π-system P and are σ-finite on P agree on σ(P). In particular a probability law on R is determined by its values on half-lines, that is, by its distribution function.

concepts.name: Outer measure
concepts.summary: μ*(E)=inf Σμ_0(A_n) over countable covers of E by algebra sets; countably subadditive on all subsets. The Carathéodory-measurable sets, those splitting every set additively, form a σ-algebra.

concepts.name: Carathéodory extension theorem
concepts.summary: A countably additive premeasure μ_0 on an algebra A extends to a measure on σ(A); the extension is built from the outer measure, and it is unique when μ_0 is σ-finite.

concepts.name: Lebesgue measure
concepts.summary: The unique measure on the Borel sets of R assigning each interval its length b−a, obtained by extending interval length from the algebra of finite disjoint interval unions.

concepts.name: Completion of a measure
concepts.summary: Adding all subsets of null sets to F and extending μ yields a complete measure space; the Lebesgue σ-algebra is the completion of the Borel σ-algebra.

concepts.name: Measurable function / random variable
concepts.summary: A map X: (Ω,F) → (S,S) with X^{-1}(B) ∈ F for every B in S. It suffices to check inverse images of a generating class, for example {X ≤ x} for real X.

concepts.name: σ-algebra generated by a random variable
concepts.summary: σ(X) = {X^{-1}(B): B Borel}, the smallest σ-algebra making X measurable. It models the information revealed by observing X; Y is σ(X)-measurable exactly when Y is a Borel function of X.

concepts.name: Indicators and simple functions
concepts.summary: Finite linear combinations Σ c_k 1_{A_k} of indicators of measurable sets. Integrals, independence and measurability are defined or checked first on simple functions.

concepts.name: Simple-function approximation
aliases: measurable functions are limits of simple functions
concepts.summary: Every nonnegative measurable X is the increasing pointwise limit of simple functions X_n = min(n, 2^{-n}⌊2^n X⌋). This underpins the definition of the integral and the standard machine.

concepts.name: Functional monotone class theorem
concepts.summary: A vector space of bounded functions containing constants and indicators of a π-system, closed under bounded increasing limits, contains all bounded σ(P)-measurable functions. A function-level analogue of π–λ.

concepts.name: Closure properties of measurable functions
aliases: sums, products, compositions, sup, inf, limsup of measurable functions
concepts.summary: Continuous and monotone maps are Borel; compositions, sums, products, countable sup, inf, limsup and liminf of measurable functions are measurable, so pointwise limits of random variables are random variables.

concepts.name: Law of a random variable
concepts.summary: The probability measure P_X(B)=P(X∈B) on the target space, the pushforward of P under X. Many results depend on X only through its law.

concepts.name: Distribution function (CDF)
concepts.summary: F_X(x)=P(X≤x): nondecreasing, right-continuous, with limits 0 at −∞ and 1 at +∞. Jumps of F are atoms of the law; continuous mass produces no jump.

concepts.name: CDF characterization theorem
concepts.summary: Any nondecreasing right-continuous F with limits 0 and 1 is the distribution function of a unique probability measure on R, constructed by extension from F(b)−F(a) on intervals or via a quantile transform.

concepts.name: Equality in law versus almost surely
concepts.summary: X and Y are equal in law when P_X=P_Y, possibly on different probability spaces; X=Y almost surely is much stronger, requiring the same space and P(X≠Y)=0.

concepts.name: Support and atoms of a law
concepts.summary: The support is the smallest closed set of full measure; an atom is a point x with P(X=x)>0, seen as a jump of the CDF. Positive mass on an interval need not create any atom.

concepts.name: Lebesgue integral
aliases: integral with respect to a measure
concepts.summary: Defined for simple functions by Σ c_k μ(A_k), for nonnegative f as the supremum over simple functions below f, and for signed f as ∫f⁺−∫f⁻ when not both are infinite.

concepts.name: Expectation
concepts.summary: E[X]=∫ X dP, the Lebesgue integral of a random variable with respect to the probability measure; linear, monotone, and defined in [−∞,∞] when E X⁺ or E X⁻ is finite.

concepts.name: Additivity of the integral
concepts.summary: E[aX+bY]=aE[X]+bE[Y] for integrable X,Y, and E[Σ X_n]=Σ E[X_n] for nonnegative X_n; proved by passing from simple functions to monotone limits.

concepts.name: Standard machine
concepts.summary: Prove an integral identity for indicators, extend by linearity to simple functions, by monotone convergence to nonnegative functions, and by splitting f=f⁺−f⁻ to integrable functions.

concepts.name: Monotone convergence theorem
concepts.summary: If 0 ≤ X_n ↑ X almost surely then E[X_n] ↑ E[X]. Limits and integrals may be exchanged for increasing nonnegative sequences, with no integrability assumption.

concepts.name: Markov inequality
concepts.summary: For nonnegative X and a>0, P(X≥a) ≤ E[X]/a; more generally P(X≥a) ≤ E[f(X)]/f(a) for nondecreasing f ≥ 0. A zero integral of a nonnegative function forces it to vanish almost everywhere.

concepts.name: Chebyshev inequality
concepts.summary: Markov's inequality applied to (X−EX)²: P(|X−EX|≥t) ≤ Var(X)/t². The workhorse bound behind L² weak laws.

concepts.name: Chernoff bound
concepts.summary: Markov's inequality applied to e^{θX}: P(X≥a) ≤ e^{−θa}E[e^{θX}], optimized over θ>0; gives exponentially small tail probabilities when the moment generating function is finite.

concepts.name: Jensen inequality
concepts.summary: For convex φ and integrable X, φ(E[X]) ≤ E[φ(X)]; proved from a supporting line (hyperplane) at E[X]. Concave functions reverse the inequality, as in E log X ≤ log E X.

concepts.name: Hölder inequality
concepts.summary: For conjugate exponents 1/p+1/q=1, E|XY| ≤ ‖X‖_p‖Y‖_q, derived from Young's inequality ab ≤ a^p/p + b^q/q; equality needs |X|^p and |Y|^q proportional.

concepts.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
concepts.summary: The case p=q=2 of Hölder: |E[XY]| ≤ (E[X²]E[Y²])^{1/2}; it bounds covariances and correlations and is the inner-product inequality of L².

concepts.name: Minkowski inequality
concepts.summary: ‖X+Y‖_p ≤ ‖X‖_p+‖Y‖_p for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, the triangle inequality making ‖·‖_p a seminorm; proved with Hölder applied to |X+Y|^{p−1}.

concepts.name: Lp spaces
concepts.summary: The random variables with E|X|^p<∞, modulo almost-sure equality, normed by ‖X‖_p=(E|X|^p)^{1/p}; quotienting turns the seminorm into a norm. Simple functions are dense for p<∞.

concepts.name: Essential supremum and L∞
concepts.summary: ‖X‖_∞ = inf{c: P(|X|>c)=0}, the smallest almost-sure bound; ‖X‖_p → ‖X‖_∞ as p→∞ on a probability space.

concepts.name: Nesting of Lp spaces
concepts.summary: On a probability space p ↦ ‖X‖_p is nondecreasing, so L^q ⊆ L^p for p ≤ q; it follows from Jensen with the convex map t ↦ t^{q/p}. Fails for infinite measures such as Lebesgue measure on R.

concepts.name: Almost sure convergence
aliases: pointwise convergence off a null set
concepts.summary: X_n → X a.s. when P({ω: X_n(ω) → X(ω)})=1; equivalently, for every ε>0, P(|X_n−X|>ε infinitely often)=0, which is a limsup-event (tail-type) statement.

concepts.name: Convergence in probability
concepts.summary: X_n → X in probability when P(|X_n−X|>ε) → 0 for every ε>0. Implied by a.s. and by Lp convergence; it implies a.s. convergence along a subsequence.

concepts.name: Convergence in Lp
concepts.summary: X_n → X in L^p when E|X_n−X|^p → 0. Markov's inequality shows it implies convergence in probability; the converse needs uniform integrability.

concepts.name: Convergence-mode counterexamples
concepts.summary: Indicators of intervals sweeping repeatedly across [0,1] converge in probability and in L^p but not almost surely; spikes n·1_{(0,1/n)} converge almost surely but not in L^1. They separate the convergence modes.

concepts.name: Fatou's lemma
concepts.summary: For nonnegative X_n, E[liminf X_n] ≤ liminf E[X_n]; proved by applying monotone convergence to the lower envelopes inf_{k≥n} X_k.

concepts.name: Dominated convergence theorem
concepts.summary: If X_n → X almost surely (or in probability) and |X_n| ≤ Y with E[Y]<∞, then E[X_n] → E[X] and E|X_n−X| → 0; proved by applying Fatou to Y±X_n.

concepts.name: Bounded convergence theorem
concepts.summary: On a probability space, if X_n → X in probability and |X_n| ≤ K, then E[X_n] → E[X]; the special case of dominated convergence with a constant dominating variable.

concepts.name: Scheffé's lemma
aliases: densities converging pointwise converge in L1
concepts.summary: If nonnegative f_n → f almost everywhere and ∫f_n → ∫f < ∞, then ∫|f_n−f| → 0; for probability densities pointwise convergence gives total-variation convergence of the laws.

concepts.name: Uniform integrability
concepts.summary: A family {X_α} is uniformly integrable when sup_α E[|X_α|; |X_α|>M] → 0 as M→∞, equivalently bounded in L^1 with uniformly small integrals over small events. Domination by one integrable variable and bounded L^p norms (p>1) are sufficient conditions.

concepts.name: Vitali convergence theorem
aliases: UI plus convergence in probability gives L1 convergence
concepts.summary: X_n → X in L^1 if and only if X_n → X in probability and {X_n} is uniformly integrable; it sharpens dominated convergence into a characterization.

concepts.name: Density-weighted measure
concepts.summary: For measurable f ≥ 0, ν(A)=∫_A f dμ defines a measure, and ∫g dν = ∫ g f dμ by the standard machine. Probability densities are the case μ = Lebesgue measure and ∫f=1.

concepts.name: Absolute continuity and Radon–Nikodym
concepts.summary: If ν ≪ μ (μ-null sets are ν-null) and μ is σ-finite, then ν has a density dν/dμ. A Dirac mass is not absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and so has no density.

concepts.name: Probability density
aliases: density of a law with respect to Lebesgue measure
concepts.summary: A nonnegative f with ∫f=1 such that P(X∈B)=∫_B f(x)dx; then E g(X)=∫ g(x) f(x) dx. Exists exactly when the law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

concepts.name: Change of variables formula
concepts.summary: E[g(X)] = ∫ g(x) P_X(dx): expectations of functions of X can be computed on the target space using only the law of X; proved by the standard machine from indicators.

concepts.name: Independence
concepts.summary: σ-algebras F_1,…,F_n are independent when P(A_1∩…∩A_n)=ΠP(A_i) for all A_i∈F_i; random variables are independent when their generated σ-algebras are. Infinite families require every finite subfamily.

concepts.name: Pairwise versus mutual independence
aliases: three fair bits with a parity constraint
concepts.summary: Two fair bits and their XOR are pairwise independent but not mutually independent: mutual independence must test every finite subfamily, not only pairs.

concepts.name: Independence from generating π-systems
concepts.summary: If π-systems P_i are independent then σ(P_i) are independent; so independence of real random variables follows from factorization of P(X_1≤x_1,…,X_n≤x_n), and disjoint groups of independent variables are independent.

concepts.name: Tail σ-algebra
concepts.summary: T = ⋂_n σ(X_n,X_{n+1},…), the events unchanged by altering finitely many coordinates, such as {Σ X_n converges} or {limsup X_n > c}.

concepts.name: Kolmogorov 0–1 law
concepts.summary: For independent X_1,X_2,…, every tail event has probability 0 or 1, because the tail σ-algebra is independent of itself; tail random variables are almost surely constant.

concepts.name: Product σ-algebra
concepts.summary: The σ-algebra on Ω_1×Ω_2 (or an infinite product) generated by measurable rectangles A_1×A_2, equivalently the smallest one making coordinate projections measurable. On R^n it equals the Borel σ-algebra.

concepts.name: Product measure
concepts.summary: There is a unique measure on the product σ-algebra with μ(A_1×A_2)=μ_1(A_1)μ_2(A_2) for σ-finite factors; countable additivity is checked on the algebra of finite disjoint rectangle unions by slicing.

concepts.name: Independence as a product law
aliases: joint law equals product of marginals
concepts.summary: Random variables are independent if and only if their joint law is the product of their marginal laws, which links probabilistic independence to the product-measure construction.

concepts.name: Kolmogorov extension theorem
aliases: existence of a process on R^N
concepts.summary: A consistent family of finite-dimensional laws on R^n, n=1,2,…, comes from a unique probability measure on the infinite product (R^N, cylinder σ-algebra); in particular infinite i.i.d. sequences exist.

concepts.name: Existence of independent sequences
aliases: constructing independent coordinates with prescribed laws
concepts.summary: Given laws μ_1, μ_2, …, there is a probability space carrying independent X_i with X_i ~ μ_i, built as coordinates of a product space (or from binary digits of one uniform variable).

concepts.name: Fubini–Tonelli theorem
concepts.summary: For f ≥ 0 measurable on a σ-finite product, ∫ f d(μ_1⊗μ_2) equals both iterated integrals (Tonelli); for f integrable the same holds with finite values (Fubini). Proved by the monotone class method from rectangles.

concepts.name: Tail-integral formula for expectations
concepts.summary: For X ≥ 0, E[X] = ∫_0^∞ P(X>t) dt and E[X^p] = ∫_0^∞ p t^{p−1} P(X>t) dt, obtained by writing X = ∫_0^∞ 1_{t<X} dt and applying Tonelli.

concepts.name: Convolution of laws
aliases: law of a sum of independent variables
concepts.summary: If X and Y are independent, the law of X+Y is μ_X * μ_Y(B)=∫ μ_X(B−y) μ_Y(dy), with density ∫ f_X(z−y) f_Y(y) dy when densities exist; computed via Fubini on the product law.

concepts.name: Variance and covariance of sums
concepts.summary: Var(Σ X_k) = Σ Var(X_k) + 2Σ_{j<k} Cov(X_j,X_k); for uncorrelated variables the cross terms vanish, and decay of covariances controls the variance of averages.

concepts.name: L² weak law of large numbers
concepts.summary: If X_k are uncorrelated with bounded variances, S_n/n − E[S_n]/n → 0 in L² and hence in probability, because Var(S_n/n) ≤ C/n.

concepts.name: Truncation
concepts.summary: Replace X_k by X_k 1_{|X_k| ≤ b_n} so second moments exist, control the variance of the truncated sum, and show the discarded part is negligible; extends weak laws to variables with only a first moment.

concepts.name: Weak law of large numbers
aliases: convergence of sample means in probability
concepts.summary: For i.i.d. integrable X_k, S_n/n → E[X_1] in probability; proved by truncation plus a second-moment bound even without finite variance.

concepts.name: Limsup events (infinitely often)
concepts.summary: limsup A_n = ⋂_n ⋃_{k≥n} A_k is the event that infinitely many A_n occur; liminf A_n is the event that all but finitely many occur. Almost sure convergence is phrased through such events.

concepts.name: First Borel–Cantelli lemma
concepts.summary: If Σ P(A_n) < ∞ then P(A_n infinitely often) = 0, with no independence assumption; proved from E[Σ 1_{A_n}] < ∞ or by continuity of measure.

concepts.name: Second Borel–Cantelli lemma
aliases: independent events with divergent sum occur infinitely often
concepts.summary: If the A_n are independent and Σ P(A_n) = ∞ then P(A_n infinitely often) = 1; independence (or a pairwise substitute) is essential.

concepts.name: Second-moment method
concepts.summary: Lower-bounds P(Z>0) ≥ (E Z)²/E[Z²] for counts Z=Σ1_{A_k}; the Kochen–Stone lemma gives P(A_n i.o.) ≥ limsup (Σ P(A_k))²/Σ_{j,k} P(A_j∩A_k) without full independence.

concepts.name: Subsequence method
concepts.summary: Prove almost sure convergence along a sparse subsequence n_k (often geometric) with summable error probabilities via Borel–Cantelli, then control fluctuations between n_k and n_{k+1} using monotonicity.

concepts.name: A.s. convergence along a subsequence
aliases: convergence in probability implies a.s. convergence along a subsequence
concepts.summary: If X_n → X in probability, there is a subsequence with X_{n_k} → X almost surely: choose n_k with P(|X_{n_k}−X|>2^{-k}) ≤ 2^{-k} and apply the first Borel–Cantelli lemma.

concepts.name: Strong law of large numbers
concepts.summary: For i.i.d. X_k with E|X_1| < ∞, S_n/n → E[X_1] almost surely; with E[X_1⁺]=∞ and E[X_1⁻]<∞ the averages tend to +∞. Proved by truncation, a variance bound on a subsequence, and Borel–Cantelli.

concepts.name: Kolmogorov maximal inequality
concepts.summary: For independent mean-zero square-integrable X_k, P(max_{k≤n}|S_k| ≥ t) ≤ Var(S_n)/t²: Chebyshev's bound holds for the whole path of partial sums, not just its endpoint.

concepts.name: Convergence of random series
concepts.summary: For independent X_n, Σ Var(X_n) < ∞ with mean-zero terms implies Σ X_n converges almost surely; the three-series theorem characterizes almost sure convergence using truncation. By the 0–1 law the probability of convergence is 0 or 1.

concepts.name: Normal distribution
concepts.summary: The law with density (2πσ²)^{-1/2} exp(−(x−μ)²/(2σ²)) and characteristic function exp(iμt − σ²t²/2); stable under independent sums and the universal limit in the central limit theorem.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.summary: For i.i.d. X_k with mean μ and finite variance σ², (S_n − nμ)/(σ√n) converges in distribution to a standard normal; the scaling √n is the size of typical fluctuations of the sum.

concepts.name: Lindeberg–Feller CLT
concepts.summary: For a triangular array of independent row entries with total variance 1, the Lindeberg condition Σ E[X_{n,k}²; |X_{n,k}|>ε] → 0 implies the row sums converge in distribution to N(0,1); Lyapunov's condition is a sufficient special case.

concepts.name: Convergence in distribution
concepts.summary: X_n ⇒ X when F_{X_n}(x) → F_X(x) at every continuity point x of F_X, equivalently E g(X_n) → E g(X) for bounded continuous g; it only concerns laws, so the X_n may live on different spaces.

concepts.name: Skorokhod representation
aliases: almost sure representation of weak convergence
concepts.summary: If X_n ⇒ X, there are Y_n =d X_n and Y =d X on one probability space with Y_n → Y almost surely, built from quantile functions of a single uniform variable; it lets a.s. tools prove distributional statements.

concepts.name: Slutsky's lemma
aliases: X_n ⇒ X and Y_n → c imply X_n + Y_n ⇒ X + c
concepts.summary: If X_n ⇒ X and Y_n → c in probability for a constant c, then X_n+Y_n ⇒ X+c and X_nY_n ⇒ cX; negligible perturbations do not change a distributional limit.

concepts.name: Weak convergence of measures
aliases: ∫ g dμ_n → ∫ g dμ for bounded continuous g
concepts.summary: Probability measures μ_n ⇒ μ when ∫g dμ_n → ∫g dμ for all bounded continuous g; the portmanteau theorem gives equivalent forms with open sets, closed sets, and μ-continuity sets.

concepts.name: Tightness and Helly selection
aliases: no escape of mass to infinity
concepts.summary: A family of laws is tight if for each ε some compact set carries mass at least 1−ε under all of them; Helly's selection theorem says every tight sequence on R has a weakly convergent subsequence.

concepts.name: Characteristic function
concepts.summary: φ_X(t) = E[e^{itX}], the Fourier transform of the law of X; it always exists, is uniformly continuous with |φ| ≤ 1, and turns convolution of independent laws into multiplication.

concepts.name: Characteristic functions and moments
concepts.summary: If E|X|^n < ∞ then φ_X is n times continuously differentiable with φ^{(k)}(0) = i^k E[X^k]; sharp bounds on the remainder of the Taylor expansion of e^{ix} control φ near 0.

concepts.name: Lévy inversion formula
aliases: the characteristic function determines the law
concepts.summary: μ((a,b)) + μ({a,b})/2 = lim_{T→∞} (2π)^{-1} ∫_{−T}^{T} (e^{−ita} − e^{−itb})/(it) φ(t) dt, so a law is determined by its characteristic function; integrable φ gives a continuous density.

concepts.name: Lévy continuity theorem
aliases: convergence of characteristic functions implies convergence in distribution
concepts.summary: X_n ⇒ X if and only if φ_{X_n}(t) → φ_X(t) for every t; if φ_{X_n} converges pointwise to a function continuous at 0, the laws are tight and converge to the law with that characteristic function.
